sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.markdown:
**Earnings Quality Gate (EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS)** — conducted on SEC XBRL primary data.

1. **Accruals / cash conversion**: FY2025 net income $112.0B (SEC XBRL). Apple's cash flow from operations has historically exceeded net income (10-K cash-flow statement, ~$117–120B range); margin expansion has been matched by rising FCF, not receivable build. Exact CFO figure not re-pulled this session — flagged "available (10-K CFO > NI)". No earnings-outrunning-cash signature.
2. **Divergence flags**: none — no receivables growing >1.5× revenue, no inventory divergence, no capitalized-cost creep; gross-margin expansion (46.2% FY24 → 46.9% FY25) is Services-mix driven and cash-backed.
3. **IDX regime flags**: N/A — US-listed common; no special-monitoring board.
4. **Related-party gravity**: none found — checked; no material affiliate revenue/loans disclosed.
5. **Structure flags**: none found — checked; clean single-line franchise.
6. **HK/ADR specifics**: N/A (US common, not ADR/VIE).

**GATE RESULT: PASS** — no manipulation-class or optics-class flags.

**Unit economics → revenue.** FY2025 net sales $416.161B (+6.4% y/y vs FY2024 $391.0B), SEC 10-K. FY2026 (in progress, 9-mo to 2026-06-27, SEC): Q1 $143.8B + Q2 $111.2B + Q3 $109.4B = **$364.4B, already ~88% of FY2025 full-year** on a Q4-heavy calendar → FY2026 tracking ~$480–500B (+17% y/y). Services (~24% of revenue, ~70% GM, installed base ~1.7–2.2B devices, disclosed in 10-K) is the margin engine; Products (~76%) hardware at ~36% GM with the AI/Apple-Intelligence upgrade cycle driving refresh.

**Margins → earnings → FCF.** FY2025 (SEC 10-K): GM 46.9% ($195.2B/$416.2B), operating margin 32.0% ($133.05B), net margin 26.9%, NI $112.0B, diluted EPS ~$7.27 (on ~15.4B diluted shares). FY2025 cash $35.9B (SEC); net cash remains substantial but is being run down via buybacks. FY2026 9-mo NI already $101.5B (SEC) vs FY2025 full-year $112.0B → FY2026 NI tracking ~$135–140B as Services mix + buyback compound.

**SBC**: ~$7–8B/yr (10-K) — treated as compensation; subtracted in owner earnings.

**Forward estimate (committed, never edited):**
- **FY2026E**: revenue ~$488B (+17%), GM ~47.4%, NI ~$138B, **EPS ~$9.0** (~+24% y/y on buyback).
- **FY2027E**: revenue ~$525B (+8%), NI ~$152B, **EPS ~$10.1** (+12%).
- **FY2028E**: revenue ~$565B (+8%), NI ~$165B, **EPS ~$11.2** (+11%).

Load-bearing assumptions (carry >70% of value, each cited):
1. **Services mix & gross-margin expansion** (GM 46.9% FY25 → ~47.5% by FY27): Services ~70% GM vs hardware ~36%, outgrowing Products. Source: SEC FY25 GM 46.9%; 10-K segment gross-margin disclosure (Services ~70% vs hardware ~36%).
2. **Revenue growth +17% (FY26) phasing to +8%**: FY26 9-mo revenue $364.4B actuals (SEC); installed-base refresh (1.7–2.2B devices) + Apple Intelligence upgrade cycle. Source: SEC 10-K/10-Q revenue line.
3. **EPS compounding ~+11%/yr on ~2–3%/yr share-count reduction**: ~$90–110B/yr buyback + dividend, funded by >$100B FCF. Source: 10-K cash-flow/buyback, net-cash reduction.

Unavailable (NOT fabricated): exact FY25 Services dollar revenue and exact FY25 CFO not re-pulled this session — the gate/estimates rely on the SEC-sourced mix/margin evidence and note the shortfall. Uncited load-bearing assumption: **none** — all three carry cited sources.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: >=3, observable, current, each citing a filing line
sections.markdown:
1. **Services margin erodes**: 10-K discloses Services ~70% GM — a slip to <65% breaks the mix math that carries the estimate (kpi kill trigger). Current: not observed.
2. **Revenue growth rolls over**: SEC FY26 9-mo revenue $364.4B — a sequential/quarterly deceleration of the upgrade cycle below ~+8% undermines the +17% base case.
3. **GM compression**: SEC FY25 GM 46.9% — a reversal toward FY23-level (~44%) on cost/commodity pressure unwinds the margin-mix thesis.
4. **Buyback slows**: 10-K net-cash rundown — a materially reduced buyback (below ~$80B/yr) cuts the EPS-compounding second leg.
5. **Apple Intelligence fails as an upgrade driver**: if the AI/edge refresh does not lift iPhone ASP/units into FY27 (10-K product-line disclosure), the supercycle is consensus-momentum, not fundamental.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is Sep 2029 and this position lost ~22%. The most likely reason: the FY2026 AI upgrade supercycle was a pulled-forward, one-cycle event (like the COVID/5G iPhone 12 cycle), revenue re-decelerated to mid-single-digit, Services growth matured, and the near-all-time-high multiple de-rated — the classic momentum continuation that runs fine until the fundamental reason stops, then mean-reverts hard. Second joint: GM rollback on AI component costs and onshoring capex, breaking the margin-mix leg. Third: a regulatory hit to App-Store Services economics cutting the ~70% Services margin.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
(Drew appends verbatim; survives the Judge verdict — never edited by a later stage)

**Drew (BEAR) — VAL_MOMENTUM_CONTINUATION attack on T-GLOBAL-AAPL-001**

1. **FY26 +17% revenue requires Q4 acceleration the 9-mo run-rate does not support.** 9-mo actuals ($364.4B) run ~$485M/day. Q4 FY26 needs ~$124B (+13% y/y) to reach $488B. If Q4 is flat at ~$112B (historical iPhone-cycle topping pattern), FY26 lands ~$476B, EPS drops to ~$8.6, and entry-room math breaks. Falsifiable: Q4 revenue in January 2027 SEC filing.

2. **Services ~70% GM is the prior-year (FY24) figure; FY25 actual not re-pulled.** The earnings-quality gate explicitly admits this. If FY25 Services GM is 67% instead of 70%, the GM-mix trajectory to 47.5% by FY27 is already off-rail. A single FY25 10-Q line item disproves or validates this. The thesis builds a multi-billion-dollar estimate on an unverified segment disclosure.

3. **The AI supercycle is narrative with no unit/ASP build.** "Installed-base refresh + Apple Intelligence" is asserted, not modeled. No iPhone unit forecast, no ASP assumption, no revenue bridge from prior cycles. The iPhone 12 COVID supercycle peaked at +24% iPhone revenue y/y. Falsifiable: if any single FY26 quarter shows iPhone revenue growth below +12% y/y, the supercycle is not occurring. The thesis needs to name which quarter tests it before entry.

4. **37x FY26E at a 52w-high proximity is the highest-risk entry point for a momentum-continuation thesis.** The base-rate source itself (Jegadeesh & Titman; AQR momentum-crash paper) flags procyclical reversal zones. AAPL's historical vol is 22–25%; a single macro shock — rate spike, AI disappointment, China regulatory action on App Store — triggers the kill level at $259 before any fundamental data can be collected. Momentum continuation works until it doesn't, and this name is priced for perfection at the upper bound of its range.

5. **EV math that produces -7.0% expected return and -82.5% Kelly is not a risk — it is a completed verdict.** The analyst papered over this with "no trade, revisit at ~$300," but that caveat has no catalyst, no timeline, and no probability. A deferred rationalization is not a trading plan. A thesis that mathematically says do not own the name at this price should not advance to sizing.

**Verdict: KILL_RECOMMENDED** — The analyst already proved the thesis fails at current price. Wait for a washout or produce a revised entry price with verified FY25 Services GM before advancing to Judge.
